title: Practical, on-demand synthesis of arbitrary stable molecules

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a platform that accepts a molecular structure, finds a workable synthesis route, executes the chemistry, and returns an isolated compound with verified identity and purity. Its intended reach includes stable, isolable targets for which no synthesis route has been published. The complete capability would integrate route discovery, reaction control, purification and analytical verification, rather than depend on a chemist supplying a target-specific procedure. The Chemputer paper describes an ambition to discover, optimize and execute new routes on demand, but does not demonstrate this full general capability.

Scope synthesis: “Arbitrary” expresses the ambition to accommodate diverse eligible molecular structures, including unfamiliar ones; it does not mean that any finite demonstration could establish coverage of every stable molecule. This entry concerns practical synthesis through whatever executable chemistry works. It does not require a permanently closed catalog of reagents or operations, or positional atom-by-atom assembly. Practical usefulness would nevertheless require explicit limits on eligible targets, available resources, production time, quantity and purity.

significance.text: If achieved, the capability would make a molecular structure an executable production request. The comparison with programmable computers is useful because it describes a shift from individually developed procedures toward a reusable platform that can carry out many different requests. The paper presents programmable, portable chemical manufacture as a future ambition; it does not establish that chemical production already has software-like generality.

Impact synthesis: Within demonstrated operating limits, researchers could order compounds by structure, including drug candidates and experimental molecules that currently require substantial synthesis development. This could reduce the effort between proposing a molecule and testing it, widen access to specialized compounds, and support faster cycles of molecular design and experiment. These benefits depend on successful production at useful quantities and purity, with acceptable turnaround time and cost.

Impact limits: Producing a drug candidate would not establish therapeutic effectiveness or safety. General synthesis would also not automatically deliver affordable manufacturing or commodity-scale tonnage. The computer analogy describes programmability, not the cost of physical inputs, equipment capacity, purification, waste handling or scale-up. Those constraints would continue to shape what could practically be ordered and manufactured.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in the supplied account is reliable integration: discovering a route to an unfamiliar eligible target, translating it into executable operations, controlling the reactions, and obtaining verified isolated product. A theoretical reachability argument that assumes suitable transformations, reagents, catalysts and process conditions does not itself supply the chemical knowledge or autonomous planning needed to accomplish those tasks. The paper explicitly identifies incomplete understanding and encoding of chemical space as a limitation on reliable coverage.

The engineering barriers include scalable hardware and sufficiently reliable execution across different reactions and conditions. The paper's universality argument depends on real-time error correction maintaining adequate step fidelity. Practical systems must therefore do more than execute instructions: they must recognize when chemistry departs from the intended route and respond effectively. The article identifies hardware scalability, error correction and incomplete reaction knowledge as obstacles beyond its theoretical framework.

Practical synthesis: For the proposed innovation, reliable reaction execution must extend through workup, separation, purification and analytical verification. A detectable amount of target is insufficient when the requested outcome is an isolated preparative quantity at specified purity. An extensible reagent and operation set is compatible with the goal, but extensibility alone cannot establish that missing chemistry can be discovered, implemented and completed within useful resource and time limits.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies a paper by Leroy Cronin, Sebastian Pagel and colleagues in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, volume 123, article e2511080123, published electronically on April 7, 2026, with DOI 10.1073/pnas.2511080123. The paper reports analysis of 117 previously physically executed synthesis routes selected from medicinal chemistry, process chemistry and total synthesis. Its examples include atropine, and the reported reaction temperatures span −45 °C to 140 °C. These results support programmable execution of selected chemistry; they do not demonstrate autonomous synthesis from arbitrary newly submitted structures.

The authors also advance a conditional theoretical universality argument: with an extensible supply of reagents, catalysts and process conditions, and sufficient real-time error correction, a Chemputer could produce any stable, isolable molecule in finite time and detectable quantity. This is a framework-dependent claim, not a reported demonstration of arbitrary-target synthesis. Detectable quantity is a weaker outcome than isolated preparative production, and a finite duration need not be a practically acceptable turnaround time.

The paper acknowledges substantial practical challenges beyond the theoretical framework, including hardware scalability, error correction and incomplete reaction knowledge. Its discussion describes most existing systems as confined to limited reaction domains. That supports a gap between selected programmable syntheses and the proposed general platform, but it does not establish the stronger assertion that no system anywhere has achieved the capability.

The supplied evidence review covered an internally identified, untruncated copy of the full main article. It did not inspect linked supplementary files, figure images or underlying analytical data, so the route count and operating range are preserved as reports supported by the article's prose rather than independently revalidated experimental results. The supplied record contains no freshness search establishing worldwide developments between the April publication and November 1, 2026. These limits leave subsequent progress and independent confirmation unresolved; they do not show that the reported results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Independent chemists submit previously unpublished, stable, isolable targets whose routes are not supplied to the platform. For each accepted target, the platform plans and executes synthesis without a human writing target-specific procedures, then returns an isolated preparative quantity with independently verified identity and purity. The demonstration should record failures and any human intervention as well as successes.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: Before target selection, specify eligibility rules, permitted feedstocks and equipment, resource limits, turnaround time, required quantities, analytical methods and purity thresholds. Define preparative scale in relation to the intended use rather than treating detectability as sufficient. These would be proposed benchmark conditions, not established standards, and they should prevent success from depending on undisclosed changes to the task after targets are submitted.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed practical boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Proposed breadth and reproducibility: Use a chemically diverse target set, report success rates and resource use, and repeat representative syntheses across runs and independent sites. Preserve enough procedural and analytical evidence to assess reproducibility and the extent of autonomous operation. Such tests could establish convincing breadth within stated boundaries; no finite target set could prove literal access to every stable molecule. Industrial-scale cost, throughput and waste performance would require additional demonstrations.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed breadth and reproducibility

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: CHEMREV-01, “A method that predicts realistic chemical outcomes before the experiment,” could improve route selection and reduce failed experiments. Prediction alone would not deliver CHEMREV-04: a platform must also execute reactions, isolate products and verify results. Conversely, a successful synthesis platform could combine prediction with experimental feedback without first solving outcome prediction in its full generality.

Roster-based comparison: CHEMREV-05, “Enzyme-level catalysts on request for arbitrary reactions,” and CHEMREV-11, “General, predictive functionalization of a chosen unactivated C–H bond in a complex molecule,” concern capabilities that could expand the available reaction toolkit. Either could make difficult routes shorter or more selective. Neither alone supplies end-to-end synthesis across arbitrary eligible targets, and CHEMREV-04 does not require every route to use either capability.

Roster-based comparison: CHEMREV-09, “Phase-pure synthesis of arbitrary designed crystalline solids,” overlaps in the ambition to turn a specified chemical target into verified material. Its emphasis is the desired crystalline phase, whereas CHEMREV-04 emphasizes stable, isolable molecular identity and purity. Making a molecule does not by itself establish control over a designed crystalline solid or its phase purity.

Roster-based comparison: CHEMREV-10, “Positional chemical manufacture of macroscopic, atomically specified matter,” concerns a distinct construction approach and product scope. CHEMREV-04 can use conventional reaction chemistry and need not position atoms individually or specify an entire macroscopic object's atomic arrangement. The supplied roster provides only CHEMREV-10's title, so this comparison establishes a conceptual distinction rather than a detailed assessment of that entry's feasibility or progress.

Roster-based comparison: CHEMREV-06, CHEMREV-07, CHEMREV-12 and CHEMREV-13 target particular industrial transformations or production economics: nitrogen fixation, multicarbon chemicals from CO2 and water, methane-to-methanol conversion, and plastics-to-monomer recycling. General molecular synthesis would not automatically satisfy their conversion, energy or cost requirements. Likewise, producing molecules would not by itself establish the superconducting properties sought in CHEMREV-03 or the battery performance sought in CHEMREV-08. CHEMREV-02 concerns open-ended evolution in a synthetic chemical system, a different capability from fulfilling specified molecular production requests.

change_log.change: Preserved CHEMREV-04's identity and expanded the concept into an integrated structure-to-product capability covering planning, execution, isolation and verification.
change_log.reason: Both the research and review distinguish the intended breakthrough from repetition of selected known procedures.

change_log.change: Removed the requirement for a permanently closed reagent and operation catalog while retaining the criticism of assumption-dependent universality.
change_log.reason: A closed catalog is an additional architectural restriction; extensible resources are compatible with practical synthesis, but do not establish autonomous chemical reachability.

change_log.change: Replaced the categorical worldwide absence claim with a dated account of what the supplied paper demonstrates.
change_log.reason: One April 2026 paper and an empty freshness record cannot establish the status of every platform on November 1, 2026.

change_log.change: Retained the 117-route count, −45 °C to 140 °C range and atropine example, and clarified that the paper analyzes previously executed, selected routes.
change_log.reason: The review supports these quantitative details in the main article's Examples section, while distinguishing them from arbitrary-target autonomous synthesis.

change_log.change: Expanded the theoretical universality conditions and distinguished detectable quantity and finite time from practical preparative production.
change_log.reason: The framework assumes extensible reagents, catalysts, process conditions and sufficient error correction; its outcome is weaker than the proposed innovation's practical requirements.

change_log.change: Retained the programmable-computer analogy as conditional impact reasoning and separated compound availability from efficacy, affordability and bulk manufacturing.
change_log.reason: The analogy explains the proposed change in programmability without implying that physical production inherits software economics or establishes downstream performance.

change_log.change: Made the completion proposal operational through predefined boundaries, independent analysis, failure reporting and reproducibility.
change_log.reason: A convincing demonstration needs reviewable success conditions, and finite testing establishes demonstrated breadth rather than literal universality.

change_log.change: Integrated source-access limitations and expanded roster-based comparisons with explicitly identified conceptual synthesis.
change_log.reason: The supplied review did not inspect supplements or underlying analytical data, and the related entries were supplied as titles rather than full evidence records.

unresolved_issues: Worldwide progress after the April 7, 2026 publication through November 1, 2026 is not established by the supplied record.
The supplementary files, figure images and underlying analytical data were not inspected in the supplied review; independent confirmation of experimental scope remains unresolved.
Target eligibility, preparative quantities, purity thresholds, acceptable turnaround time, resource limits and permitted human intervention remain to be specified for a concrete benchmark.
The supplied evidence does not establish how broadly autonomous route discovery, error correction, purification and verification can be integrated for targets without published routes.
The other roster entries were supplied only by ID and title, limiting detailed assessment of their overlap, feasibility and current progress.
